[CGL Tier II 13/9/2019]
questions.s: "Worst" is the superlative form, used when comparing more than two things. "Worse" is comparative, used for comparing two things. Therefore, "the worst" is correct.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution.’
o: is the elder
is the oldest
is the old
questions.s:
Answer: c) is the oldest

Explanation:
Both “eldest” and “oldest” are superlative forms of “old,” but:

  • “Oldest” is more commonly used in general contexts to describe the person or thing with the greatest age.

  • “Eldest” is traditionally used within families or groups of related people.

Since the sentence refers to “the eldest member of our town” (a general group, not necessarily family), “oldest” is the more appropriate and widely accepted choice here.

Correct sentence:
“She is the oldest member of our town.”

Other options are incorrect because:

  • “is the elder” – comparative, not superlative

  • “is the old” – grammatically incorrect

  • No substitution – acceptable but less common in this context

Hence, option (c) is the best choice.

questions.s: The error is in part (b). The adverb should be 'hardly,' not 'hard,' in this context. Answer: (b). Adverb 'hardly' chahiye, 'hard' galat hai. Jawab: (b).

o: The adjustments we have to make
Because we have been used to
This will be most difficult of
questions.s: The superlative 'most difficult' requires the article 'the' before it. Correct is "the most difficult".

questions.q: Ramesh wanted to go farther into the forest to explore its depths.
questions.s:
The sentence "Ramesh wanted to go farther into the forest to explore its depths." is grammatically correct, but let's refine the usage of "farther" vs. "further."

Explanation:

  • "Farther" is used for physical distance (e.g., "He walked farther down the road").
  • "Further" is used for figurative or abstract distance (e.g., "Let's discuss this further").

Since "into the forest" refers to physical distance, "farther" is correctly used here.

questions.q: (a) My all /(b) friends will come /(c) tomorrow to meet me /(d) no error.
Which of the following CANNOT be put under the classification of adjectives?
questions.s:
On the basis of how adjectives describe a noun/pronoun, they are classified as:

• Adjectives of Quality - describes kind or quality of a person or thing.

• Adjectives of Quantity - shows how much of a thing is meant.

• Adjectives of Number - shows how many persons or things are meant, or in what order a person or thing stands.

• Demonstrative Adjectives - points out which person or thing is meant.

• Interrogative Adjectives - used with nouns to ask questions.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.q: She wrote me an (anguished) letter from her prison cell.
questions.s: The word “anguished” describes the noun “letter”, so it functions as an adjective.

questions.q: The Federalists wished to / make the central government /as strong possible. (SSC MTS Tier-01 12/05/23)
questions.s: The correct correlative construction for comparison is "as strong as possible".

questions.q: If he wants / farther information, / send him / to me.
questions.s: Explanation:- (a) use ‘further’ instead of ‘farther’ kyunki farther ka use distance ko refer karne ke liye kiya jaata hai jabki 'further' ka use more/addition ko refer karne ke liye kiya jaata hai.

questions.q: Illegal sand mining has become (a)/ a boom business fuelled (b)/ by the ever- increasing demand (c)/ of the construction industry. (d)/ No error (e)
questions.s: Use "booming business" (present participle as adjective) instead of "boom business."

questions.q: Love is the_______thing in the world.
questions.s: Love” is being compared with everything in the world, so we need the superlative degree of the adjective. So, most important is the correct form.

questions.q: She is (a) / more prettier (b) / than her sister. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Prettier' is already comparative, so 'more' is redundant. Correct form is 'prettier than.' Answer: (b). 'Prettier' pehle se comparative hai, toh 'more' extra hai. Sahi form hai 'prettier than.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q: The militants (a)/entered the palace (b)/from the utmost gate (c)/with guns hidden in their clothes. (d)
She is (a) / more beautiful (b) / than her cousin. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: There is no error. 'More beautiful' is correct for comparative degree. Answer: (d). Sentence mein koi galti nahi, 'more beautiful' comparative degree ke liye sahi hai. Jawab: (d).

questions.q:
Sakshi is as smarter as any other child in the class.

[MTS 13/8/2019 S1]
questions.s: "Smarter" is a comparative adjective, but "as...as" is used with the positive degree of an adjective

questions.q: We've got (a new big house).
questions.s:
Adjectives follow a fixed order:
Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Colour → Origin → Material → Purpose + Noun. So size comes before age.
